newsitem.title: UK: Britain to review Railtrack regulation.
newsitem.headline: Britain to review Railtrack regulation.

text.p: Britain's new Labour Government said on Wednesday it would review options to toughen the regulation of privatised rail companies such as Railtrack Plc.
"The regulation of the rail industry, and the sanctions available to the regulators, need to be strengthened," Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott said in a statement.
Prescott's statement followed news that Britain's railway regulator planned to amend Railtrack's licence to make sure the company delivered on its investment plans.
"Railtrack receives vast amounts of public money each year," Prescott said.
"We need a system of regulation which guarantees that this money is spent in the public interest, on facilities and services which benefit the travelling public and railfreight customers," he added.
He said the government's review would be in line with its plans to introduce a strategic rail authority.
Earlier, Railtrack said it was delivering on its promises, which include plans to spend 1.0 billion stg to upgrade 2,500 stations across Britain.
The plan, launched on Tuesday, followed last year's public rebuke from Rail Regulator John Swift, who criticised Railtrack's delays in investment.
Railtrack said the station improvement plan was part of a commitment to spend 16 billion stg in 10 years on improvement to its entire infrastructure. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
